title: NO KINGS- Winchester

location.venue: Sidewalk in front of Winchester Unitarian Society

description:
**In America, we don’t put up with would-be kings.**

IndivisibleWIN will join activists across the country for
a coordinated "No Kings" standout, a powerful display of civic resistance demanding accountability, justice, and the preservation of American democracy.

Participants will gather peacefully from 10:30 AM to 12:00 PM on the sidewalk in front of the Winchester Unitarian Society. Everyone is encouraged to bring 2 or 3 friends and join us with signs for a high-visibility action. 

We’ve seen courts ignored, communities torn apart, rights under attack, and vital services slashed. But we know the power of the
people is greater than any one person’s grip on power. We’re standing together to defend our democracy — no thrones, no crowns, no kings — just a government that serves us all.

This standout is part of a nationwide movement affirming that power in America belongs to the people — not to any individual or dynasty.
Check out nokings.org for more information.

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

title: We Have No Kings In America!
description:
On Flag Day, June 14, 2025 in Dripping Springs, at 10 am, we shall once again gather under the big oaks at the picnic tables at Veterans Park in Downtown Drippin' to exercise our First Amendment Rights.

In light of the fact that "someone" is having a big, unAmerican and very expensive military parade in D.C. that same day, we are going to celebrate our flag and our freedom in our own way, with signs, banners, FLAGS and our cars, painted up like it's Prom Night.  

Our celebration of Freedom and our Rights as Americans will begin, as it does every Saturday morning, with a march to the intersection of RR 12 and Hwy 290 West, to OCCUPY the four corners with our signs and flags flying, while we wave to our neighbors passing by.  

We will also be handing out pocket-sized copies of the U.S. Constitution, just in case some of our neighbors would like to compare what is going on these days, with what the Founding Fathers had in mind.

We have been greeted most Saturdays by friendly waves, thumbs up and honks, but there are always a few who for some reason think we should not be expressing ourselves.  We wave and smile at them, too!

Then, around noonish, we will once again gather under the oaks to organize ourselves into a caravan of cars and trucks, flying our flags, and adorn our vehicles with white shoe polish in the time-honored tradition of Prom Night, weddings and winning the State Championship.  

We will do a little dance around town, our very own version of a Flag Day Parade, then making our way to one of the local watering holes to hoist a cold one, and get some lunch.  Stay tuned for details.

Street theater, costumes, music and dancing is encouraged, as are American flags, PRIDE flags, signs, banners, songs, chants, and dance. 

We invite you to bring anything that helps you to express how you feel about being an American, and how you are not amused at how the current Administration is abusing their power, and wasting our tax dollars marching tanks and soldiers down Pennsylannia Avenue.

Be sure to dress for the summer weather, bring water, snacks, a sun hat, comfy shoes and your love of Democracy.

See you all on June 14, starting at 10 am at Veterans Park in DownTown Dripping Springs, Texas!

title: Summer to Grow, Turn up the Heat - Absorbing our People Training
description:
*note - these are stand alone, identical trainings and not a series! read more below to learn more!*

This summer it's time turn up the heat! 

Come join us for a training on absorption so we can get oriented toward growing our movement and building our skills to effectively welcome thousands of new people into SURJ! 

### Who is this training for? 

- Anyone who wants to learn about absorption and build your skills to effectively bring people into our movement in times of political activation, and anyone who is planning on hosting a mass meeting this summer! 

### What is absorption?

- Absorption is both an *orientation* toward using moments of political activation to bring more people into a movement, and it's also the skills that go along with growing our movements effectively. 

### Why do we absorb?

- We absorb because in order to achieve our goals, we need to use solidarity power (the ability to work and act together as a collective) to move large amounts of people to to build the world we want to see. In order to harness solidarity power, we must always be growing our movements and welcoming more people to move and take action with us. 

### This training will cover: 

- SURJ’s long-term strategy and goals, and why we organize white people

- SURJ's plan to support members, circles and chapters to host mass meetings throughout the summer to welcome more people into our movement

- The fundamentals of absorption: the whys, how tos, best practices, and how to create an absorption plan grounded in your context

- Examples of absorption successes and fails

- Next steps for getting involved, doing your own absorption, and hosting a mass meeting.

We are offering three absorption trainings on June 12th, 18th and 26th. These are STAND ALONE trainings and they are not a series. We will be offering the SAME training on each of these dates to offer people different scheduling options for attending, so you only need to sign up for ONE of these trainings!

description:

Title: Of the People, By the People, For the People- Protest March and Rally

Theme: Attack Our Problems, Embrace Our Neighbors

Diversity makes our nation stronger! Division is our weakness, and the Mega Rich Oligarchs know it. Join us, the 99%, to condemn federal attacks on and show our appreciation for foreign students, immigrants, the LGBTQIA+ community, Native Americans, Black Americans, Latino Americans, Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders, working poor, homeless, those on disability, veterans, the elderly, federal workers and more. The time to speak up is NOW!!! No more parties, no more politics, no kings. The time to stand up is NOW! Someone you care about is already affected. Who will be next?

Where and When:
March Route- Meet at 3:30 pm on either side of the old Flathead County Courthouse (800 S Main St, Kalispell). Rally at Depot Park @4-5:30 pm.

We will proceed along both sides of Main Street to Depot Park. We’ll be walking on the sidewalks so please make sure there’s a space for people who aren’t protesting to pass. We also need to follow all traffic laws, no blocking traffic, obeying crosswalk lights, and staying on the sidewalk.

If you can’t walk from the courthouse, there will be a crew at Depot Park for the duration of the event so plan to stay there.

Rally Details- The rally ends at Depot Park in Kalispell! This is where we’ll have speakers, music, and food (more on that later) from 4-5:30 pm. After the rally, you can stay and visit or walk back to the courthouse at your leisure.

Safety notes: There will likely be a few counter protesters, although we’ve taken steps to minimize this risk. Please just ignore them. There will be a few folks on hand to help deescalate potential conflicts but since there will be so many of us, it’s helpful if we commit to supporting one another and NOT engaging with trolls.

We’ll be in Depot Park so do your best to tread lightly on the grass and to clean up. This is our chance to demonstrate that we’re a respectful and upstanding group–neighbors and friends who are standing up for our country.

Parking and bathrooms: There’s parking on the east and west sides of the old courthouse and in the surrounding neighborhoods. If you’re meeting at Depot Park, you can park at the Mall or the Super 1. Please only park in the Depot Park parking lot if you are elderly or disabled.

Depot Park bathrooms will be available!

Food: We will have a drink and food table with “Resistance Swag” and voter registration at Depot Park. If you would like to donate drinks, side dishes or desserts, please drop them off at Depot Park at 3:00 pm. If you know any businesses that might want to donate and you can reach out and coordinate we’d appreciate it! Thanks in advance!

These notes are also important!

Email flatheaddemocracy@gmail.com with questions or if you're interested in volunteering for logistics or donating food/supplies!

Bring cash! We’ll have a table setup for some swag and appreciate donations to cover printing costs, as well as the event permit and sound system. We’re going old school on this one and will have a donation jar. Even a couple bucks helps cover costs.

Please bring a poster (or more!) sharing what group of people you are most passionate about protecting or how diversity makes us stronger. We will have some poster making materials at the beginning if you can’t, but they will be limited. If you have extra materials to share that’s helpful too!

Wear red, white, and blue to demonstrate solidarity. This isn’t a must but it makes for a really impressive visual!

Thank you for reading all this to help us prepare together and get pumped! We are making history together ✊🏽

Best, The Whole Flathead Democracy Team

description:
## Honk & Wave 
### Pop Up Protest!

Doing this already? Want to get started? Lots of Fun, Builds Public Awareness, and you can make new local friends.

We're gearing up for June 14th No Kings Day! East Portland will have a Big Square Mile Protest the morning of 6/14 Details here: https://www.mobilize.us/nokings/event/793933/

**Anytime between Now and 6/14 - You can host a Pop-Up. Choose a busy intersection near you** for an hour or maybe 90 min. Lots of us like to gather for a snack and conversation afterwards. Include your Time and Place Details on this sign up and we'll post them for other volunteers to meet up with you.

Really helpful Sign Messaging suggestions from our No Kings Toolkit.
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1zcf6uVEMBLGwPegGZ2_tCGBzt9CBGEYateOqrLwvoQM/edit?usp=sharing

We're encouraging people to join us. Pointing out some of the many harms this authoritarian power grab has already set in motion. Showing our friends and neighbors how we can all take action.

Do post your action on your socials #NoKings #NoKingsDay #Indivisible

description:
Our rights are under attack. Our democracy is under siege. We’ve been here before, and we know what to do.

On July 17, we honor the anniversary of the passing of civil rights hero John Lewis, not with ceremonies, but with action. Across the country, we will take to the streets, courthouses, and community spaces to carry forward his fight for justice, voting rights, and dignity for all.

This is more than a protest, it’s a moral reckoning. A continuation of the movement Lewis helped lead, and a new front in the struggle for freedom.

**Please note:** a core principle behind our John Lewis Good Trouble Day actions is a commitment to nonviolence in all we do. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.
